the-36x18-member-is-the-track-label-and-.note: the two-size group is 1 label + 3 buttons, constant across heights

detail.howTheyAreIdentified: all four inherit `data-director-track-label=<track>` from the row ancestor. The nearest-data rule therefore attributes FOUR controls of TWO sizes to ONE key.

none-of-the-four-members-carries-a-data-.note: this is why 683 saw a two-size key — and it is containment, not identity

detail.correctionTo683: 683's READING stands: two data keys each carry two sizes at every height. What was wrong is the interpretation — I called it '673's 异类合并, size-side', implying an anomaly. It is the normal anatomy of a track row: one label button plus three icon buttons.
detail.historyRule: historic batches are not rewritten; the correction is recorded here, and 683 stays as it was committed
detail.whatIsStillTrue: the two-size-per-key fact, and the reusable inference below

this-is-the-anatomy-of-a-track-row-not-a.note: a fact can be right and its name wrong — the reading survives, the label does not

detail.inference: To tell whether several members under one key are INSTANCES OF ONE CLASS or A CONTAINER AND ITS CHILDREN, compare their box sizes and class roles — which is exactly the quantity 683 already measured. 683 measured the right thing; I named it wrong.
detail.alsoExplains674: 674's 'irreducible 4' has the same cause: the three nav buttons have no per-node data attribute at all, so the nearest-data rule lends them the track's key and they are necessarily equal. 674 said 'not claimed to be a lower bound' — this is WHY it is not.
detail.toBreakItApart: give the three nav buttons their own data-*; that is a change to src/ — PRODUCT DECISION

the-reusable-inference-a-container-key-v.note: this is the actionable output of the batch
